criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a new test builds fixture records in a temp directory (a rejected job with an introspection record) and shows that retrying it yields a reading input whose request carries the proposed_request, cause and prevention, the original request and the accepted corrections.
criteria.evidence: a_retry_starts_from_the_introspection_and_shows_earlier_cases_and_tried_preventions passed. It builds a Fixture (temp repo), rejects two jobs with scripted introspections, calls athena.retry, and checks that the reader brief contains the proposed request, cause, PREVENTION, '> remove the readme again' and '> name the file README.md'.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a fixture test shows earlier cases of the same class (ids and one-line what) appear in the retry's reader brief, and that a prevention already tried in an earlier introspection of the same class is shown as already tried.
criteria.evidence: The same test checks for first_case (the earlier introspection's id), '(job ', the what-happened line, 'This is case 2 of its class' and 'Prevention already tried: > code-check: Refuse a candidate'. It passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a fixture test shows `retry` on a job that is not rejected or failed is refused with a clear message. A second shows a job with no introspection falls back to the 'try again on' behavior.
criteria.evidence: a_job_that_is_not_rejected_or_failed_is_refused checks for the error 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again' and that HEAD is unchanged. a_job_with_no_introspection_falls_back_to_try_again_on checks seeded == false, that '# Earlier attempt' is present and that '# Why it happened' is absent. Both passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -- retry --help`: the command exists and takes a job argument, with the same --yes and --json options as `ask`.
criteria.evidence: The command as written fails with 'could not determine which binary to run' because the workspace has two binaries (athena and xtask); this was already so before the change. With --bin athena, the output is 'Usage: athena retry [OPTIONS] <JOB>' with --yes and --json, matching ask's --yes and --json. The test the_retry_command_takes_a_job_and_the_same_options_as_ask also checks this, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs has a `Retry` subcommand that goes through the same reading display as `ask`, and does not submit the run unless the user accepts.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: Command::Retry calls athena.retry and then show_proposal. show_proposal is the code moved out of Ask, which Ask now calls too. A run starts only through prompt_loop (Enter) or --yes (accepted by flag). Athena::retry only calls ask, and the test checks that the producer count does not change and the job state is Proposed.

criteria.criterion: The reader brief text in athena-context includes the cause, prevention and earlier-case section only when the retry came from an introspection record, with a test of that.
criteria.evidence: In briefs.rs, retry_cause_section is written only when attempt.introspection is Some. The unit test reader_briefs_carry_the_cause_and_earlier_cases_only_for_an_introspected_retry checks that the section is absent without the introspection and present with it. It passed.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new command, and README or CLI docs mention `athena retry <job>` if they list commands.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under Added. README.md has a new paragraph and a row in the command table for `athena retry <job> [--yes]`.

findings.summary: The README's command table row for `retry` lists only `[--yes]`. The command also takes `--json`, which the paragraph above the table mentions.
findings.evidence: The row reads '`athena retry <job> [--yes]`', while the help output shows --json.

findings.summary: The 'Why it happened' section is also added when the user types "try again on <job>", because earlier_attempt always fills in introspection. So it does not appear only for `athena retry`. The changelog states this; the reading's criterion 6 can be read either way.
findings.evidence: `attempt.introspection = retry_cause(records, job, redactor)?;` runs for every "try again on" request.

findings.summary: The cited command `cargo run -- retry --help` cannot run here, because the workspace has two binaries and no default-run setting. This is not caused by the candidate.
findings.evidence: error: `cargo run` could not determine which binary to run ... available binaries: athena, xtask

summary: I'm passing this change: `athena retry <job>` does what you asked. It records "try again on <job>" and adds a "Why it happened" section to the reader's brief. That section carries the job's cause, prevention and proposed next request, and lists the earlier cases of the same class (id, job, one line on what happened). It shows each earlier case's prevention as already tried. The original request and the accepted corrections still come through the existing retry path. The command uses the same reading display as `ask`, accepts `--yes` and `--json`, and runs nothing unless you accept. A job that isn't rejected or failed is refused. A job with no usable introspection falls back to plain "try again on" and prints a note on standard error. I ran the full test suite, the 5 new fixture tests, the new reader-brief unit test, clippy and fmt; all passed. One snag: `cargo run -- retry --help`, as written in criterion 4, fails because the workspace has two binaries (athena and xtask). That was true before this change too. `cargo run --bin athena -- retry --help` works and shows the job argument and both options. Two minor findings, neither blocking: the new section also appears when you type "try again on <job>" yourself (the changelog says so), and the README's command table omits `--json` for `retry`.
